titulo: The imperfect subjunctive: A first look at «se» + imperfect subjunctive

aula.objetivo: Form the imperfect subjunctive (falasse, comesse, partisse, tivesse, fosse, fizesse, viesse…) and use it after wishes, requests and doubts that lie in the past, after «como se» and in the first conditional sentences with «se».

sessao.titulo: A first look at «se» + imperfect subjunctive

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: you will meet the imperfect subjunctive in its best-known job: after «se» (if), to imagine a situation that is not true now or is unlikely. The other half of the sentence uses the conditional of lesson 41. STEP 2: the pattern is «Se» + imperfect subjunctive, conditional: «Se eu tivesse tempo, viajaria», «Se eu fosse você, aceitaria», «Se ele pudesse, viria». STEP 3: the order of the two halves can change. Without the comma: «Eu viajaria se tivesse tempo». STEP 4: in speech, many Brazilians use the imperfeito in the second half: «Se eu tivesse tempo, eu viajava». It is natural and friendly. STEP 5: «fosse» is used both for «ser» and for «ir», so «Se eu fosse a São Paulo» (if I went to São Paulo) and «Se eu fosse médico» (if I were a doctor) share one form. STEP 6: the complete system of hypotheses (real, unreal and past) is the subject of lesson 47. Today, you only need to recognise the pattern and say a few sentences.
blocos.comparacao: English says «If I had time, I would travel» and «If I were you, I would accept». The Portuguese pattern is almost word for word: «Se eu tivesse tempo, viajaria», «Se eu fosse você, aceitaria». The big difference is that you have to build the verb after «se» with the rules from today.

exemplos.pt: If I had time, I would travel.
If I were you, I would accept.
If she could, she would come.
If we knew, we would let you know.

erros.motivo: An imagined situation uses the imperfect subjunctive after «se».
The conditional goes only in the result half; after «se» use the imperfect subjunctive.

blocos.ru: Quando eu era adolescente, meus pais queriam que eu estudasse medicina. Eles esperavam que eu fosse médico, como meu avô. Mas eu sonhava que a música fosse minha profissão. Um dia, meu professor pediu que eu tocasse num concerto da escola. Meus pais vieram, e depois do concerto eles me olharam como se eu fosse outra pessoa. Foi a primeira vez que eles duvidaram que a medicina fosse o melhor caminho para mim. Hoje eu sou professor de música, e minha mãe sempre pede que eu toque a sua canção favorita.
blocos.pt: When I was a teenager, my parents wanted me to study medicine. They expected me to be a doctor, like my grandfather. But I dreamed that music would be my profession. One day, my teacher asked me to play at a school concert. My parents came, and after the concert they looked at me as if I were a different person. It was the first time they doubted that medicine was the best path for me. Today I am a music teacher, and my mother always asks me to play her favorite song.

perguntas.pergunta: What did the parents want the narrator to study? (answer in Portuguese)
Who asked the narrator to play at a concert? (answer in Portuguese)
How did the parents look at the narrator after the concert? (answer in Portuguese)
perguntas.resposta: Como se ele fosse outra pessoa.

perguntas.pergunta: What does the narrator do today? (answer in Portuguese)

blocos.enunciado: Write three sentences about your own past: what your parents or teachers wanted («queriam que…»), what you hoped («eu esperava que…») and one «se» sentence («Se eu tivesse…»).
Say three past wishes with «Eu queria que…», «Meus pais esperavam que…» and «Eu pedi que…», each with the imperfect subjunctive.
